articles.title: Lauren Sánchez Bezos-backed fund commits $4.8 million to 48 climate solutions that missed Earthshot Prize finals; funding supports projects ranging from carbon removal to wildlife protection
articles.summary: The Bezos Earth Fund, chaired by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, with Lauren Sanchez Bezos serving as vice chair, has committed $4.8 million over three years
articles.body: The Bezos Earth Fund, chaired by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, with Lauren Sanchez Bezos serving as vice chair, has committed $4.8 million over three years to support 48 climate and nature solutions nominated for the Earthshot Prize but not selected as finalists. Announced on February 4, 2026, the initiative is a collaboration between the Bezos Earth Fund and the Earthshot Prize to help promising environmental projects expand their operations and increase their impact. The programme will support 16 organisations each year, with each organisation in the first cohort receiving $100,000. The selected organisations work across areas including carbon removal, wildlife conservation, ecosystem restoration and sustainable technology. The initiative aims to extend funding opportunities beyond the prize's annual finalists and winners.Bezos Earth Fund commits $4.8 million to climate and nature solutionsThe three-year partnership will draw from the Earthshot Prize's global pool of nominees who did not make the final shortlist. The Bezos Earth Fund will provide $4.8 million in total, supporting 16 organisations annually with grants of $100,000 each.The funding is intended to help selected organisations scale their work and reach more communities, ecosystems and industries. The initiative brings together the Earthshot Prize's international network of environmental innovators and the Bezos Earth Fund's philanthropic resources to help promising solutions progress beyond their existing scale.Dr Kelly Levin, chief of science, data and systems change at the Bezos Earth Fund, said promising innovations often remain small when the world needs them to expand. She said the partnership could help these ideas grow into solutions capable of delivering wider environmental benefits.Jason Knauf, chief executive of the Earthshot Prize, said the prize's wider nomination pool represents a global pipeline of environmental innovators and potential solutions. The collaboration will allow the organisations to support additional projects beyond the prize's annual selection process.The first 16 organisations selected for fundingThe first cohort includes organisations working on carbon removal, cleaner industrial processes, wildlife protection, habitat restoration and other environmental challenges. Each will receive $100,000 to help expand its operations and amplify its impact.1. Air Protein, Inc.Air Protein develops alternative proteins using microorganisms and processes that use carbon dioxide as a feedstock. Its approach explores ways to produce protein without relying entirely on conventional agriculture and livestock farming.2. Climatenza SolarClimatenza Solar is among the first cohort of selected organisations. Its inclusion places it within the initiative's wider effort to support climate-focused innovation, although the announcement does not specify the particular solar technology or project the grant will support.3. Instituto Floresta VivaInstituto Floresta Viva is a Brazilian environmental organisation associated with Atlantic Forest conservation and restoration. Its work provides a nature-restoration angle within a programme designed to help environmental solutions expand.4. Forum Konservasi LeuserForum Konservasi Leuser works on protecting the Leuser Ecosystem in Indonesia, an important rainforest landscape in Sumatra that provides habitat for threatened wildlife. Its conservation work is linked to safeguarding forests and biodiversity.5. Fundación Rewilding ArgentinaThe Argentine conservation organisation works to protect and restore ecosystems, recover native wildlife and establish protected areas. Its projects include rewilding initiatives and efforts to reconnect habitats while supporting local economies linked to nature.6. Hyperion RoboticsHyperion Robotics develops robotic construction technology designed to reduce waste and the carbon footprint of infrastructure. Its approach focuses on improving how concrete foundations are designed and built, including for energy and industrial infrastructure.7. InPlanetInPlanet works on enhanced rock weathering, a carbon-removal approach that involves spreading finely crushed silicate rock on agricultural land to accelerate natural chemical reactions that remove carbon dioxide. The process can also improve soil conditions by releasing minerals and helping correct soil acidity.8. LassoLasso is associated with technology for recovering and recycling materials, including plastics. Its work offers a potential route to reducing waste and recovering resources that would otherwise be discarded.9. articles.summary: Kochi: The Keralam govt has removed S.
articles.body: Kochi: The Keralam govt has removed S. Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar as Kochi City District Police Chief amid mounting allegations of police lapses in the handling of the Cheranalloor fatal car crash case, in which a 55-year-old man was killed by a speeding luxury car allegedly driven by the 17-year-old son of an additional judge.Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan signed the order on Wednesday , acting on a recommendation from the Home Department. R. Nishanthini, currently serving as IGP (South Zone), is likely to succeed Kumar, who is yet to be given a new posting.The removal follows the suspension on Tuesday of four officers attached to the Cheranalloor police station. The suspended officers are station house officer and sub-inspector Viswajith V S, circle inspector Syam Kumar K S, grade ASI Manoj K T and senior civil police officer Arun Joshy. Jayabalakrishnan, who ran a roadside eatery, was reportedly heading home when the accident occurred around 2.20 am.Home minister Ramesh Chennithala had told the assembly that there had been serious police lapses and that he had personally reprimanded the director general of police after learning that the FIR had not initially included the charge of culpable homicide. A team of officers led by ADGP (law and order) P Vijayan visited the accident site and the victim’s family in Kochi on Tuesday, as directed by the minister.Vijayan held discussions with senior Kochi city police officers, including commissioner Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar, for nearly two hours on Tuesday. He also visited the accident site at Maraparambu on Container Road and briefly spoke to a watchman who was present at the spot. Both Ramesh and Vijayan said the law would take its course irrespective of persons involved.Addressing media, Vijayan had said that the police had already moved the court seeking to revoke the bail granted to the juvenile by the concerned magistrate. When asked about the possibility of an arrest of the judge, as he was arrayed as an accused, he said that it was a matter that involved multiple legal formalities, including obtaining the requisite permission from the judiciary.Meanwhile, the arrival of a separate team from the state capital is widely interpreted as a sign of the authorities' dissatisfaction with the city police's handling of the investigation.The family of the victim had also staged another protest at the station on Monday night, but called it off after Ramesh assured a fair investigation. They had warned that they would resume the protest if their demands were not met by 4 pm on Tuesday.Meanwhile, an overnight search at the judge's apartment in Aluva continued for several hours until Wednesday morning. Police have collected CCTV footage from the premises and seized documents relating to the luxury car involved in the crash and a premium motorcycle. Footage purportedly showing the car being driven out of the apartment had earlier circulated widely on social media.The police had initially registered a case against the minor driver under Sections 281 and 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to rash driving and causing death by a rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide. The teenager was subsequently released on station bail under Section 8 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.Jayabalakrishnan, who ran a roadside eatery, was heading home after closing the shop when the accident occurred at 2.20 am on Sunday. Both vehicles were travelling towards Kalamassery.Police had evidence that the car had travelled at over 100 kmph sometime before the accident, and Section 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and charges for speeding were added. articles.title: Delhi to Haridwar in 90 minutes? What Nitin Gadkari said
articles.summary: The journey from Delhi to Haridwar may soon become significantly shorter, with a new road project scheduled to open next month, union road hransport and
articles.body: The journey from Delhi to Haridwar may soon become significantly shorter, with a new road project scheduled to open next month, union road hransport and Highways minister Nitin Gadkari said on Tuesday. Once operational, the route could bring travel time down to around 90 minutes.Speaking at the Confederation of Indian Industry’s (CII) National Conference on ‘Highways of India’s Future: Smart, Safe and Sustainable’, Gadkari said the expansion of the country’s road network was making religious destinations more accessible while supporting tourism and job creation.Pointing to the recently opened Delhi-Dehradun corridor, the minister said the journey between the two cities, which earlier took about seven hours, could now be completed in roughly two hours.He said the upcoming Delhi-Haridwar project would further improve access to one of the country’s prominent pilgrimage destinations, according to ET.Gadkari also cited road development work in Ayodhya and Maharashtra, including the Pandharpur Palkhi Marg projects, which are intended to make journeys easier for devotees. He said infrastructure development was being undertaken across regions, with roads, tunnels and bridges being built in the Northeast, Jammu and Kashmir and other parts of the country.Expressways to open up new economic opportunitiesGadkari said greenfield expressways could bring regions with limited economic opportunities closer to major business centres, helping expand development beyond established urban hubs.The Delhi-Mumbai Expressway, he said, would improve access for rural areas, aspirational districts and tribal regions. In Haryana, the project is expected to benefit aspirational districts, while Alwar, Dausa, Sawai Madhopur and Bundi in Rajasthan are among the areas that could gain from improved road links.He also pointed to Ratlam and Jhabua in Madhya Pradesh and Dahod in Gujarat, highlighting the potential for better connectivity to encourage economic activity in tribal districts.Stressing the importance of the Delhi-Mumbai route, Gadkari said stronger links between the national capital and Mumbai were crucial, given the latter’s position as the country’s economic hub.100 invested in infrastructure can create 325 economic impact: GadkariThe minister said infrastructure spending has benefits beyond the construction of roads, as projects generate employment and increase demand for cement, steel and construction equipment.He added that improved connectivity could lower transportation costs and make the movement of goods and people more efficient. These gains, he said, could benefit businesses, tourism and the development of towns.Describing infrastructure as a key driver of economic growth, Gadkari said every 100 invested in the sector could produce an economic impact of 325.“If we spend 100 on infrastructure, the impact on the economy comes to 325. GDP is also going to increase,” he said.Gadkari added that the government was continuing to focus on expressways and greenfield highways to improve links between regions, strengthen economic activity and support development across India.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'We don't want a fight': Delhi traders' body writes to Rahul Gandhi again over November 1 rally
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A Delhi traders' body on Wednesday wrote another letter to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, urging him to postpone the INDIA bloc's November 1
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A Delhi traders' body on Wednesday wrote another letter to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, urging him to postpone the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan until after Diwali over fears that the gathering could disrupt business in several major markets.The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI), which has raised concerns about the rally's impact on festive sales, also sought a 20-minute meeting with Gandhi to explain why traders want the event deferred.In the letter, CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said representatives of 20 markets wanted an opportunity to put forward their concerns about the rally, which is expected to draw around 10 lakh people."We don't want a fight; we want dialogue. Rahul ji himself says that he listens to everyone, listens to the voice of small traders. So, we traders from 20 markets are asking him for 20 minutes. This will be the beauty of democracy," Goyal said.The traders' body also proposed that it would withdraw its protest if Gandhi could convince its representatives that the rally would bring more customers and boost business. However, if traders were able to convince him that the event would result in losses, they wanted him to agree to postpone it until after Diwali.Wednesday's letter was the second sent by CTI to Gandhi within four days. The organisation had first approached the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha on October 24, seeking postponement of the rally to prevent disruptions during one of the busiest periods for Delhi's markets.According to CTI, at least 20 markets within a 1-5 km radius of Ramlila Maidan could be affected by the expected turnout.The markets include Chandni Chowk, Bhagirath Palace, Khari Baoli, Sadar Bazar, Chawri Bazar, Kashmere Gate, Nabi Karim, Karol Bagh, Ajmeri Gate and Daryaganj.Nai Sarak, Kinari Bazar, Dariba Kalan, Fatehpuri, Naya Bazar, Filmistan, Paharganj, Gaffar Market, Jama Masjid-Meena Bazar and Lajpat Rai Market are also among the commercial areas identified by the traders' body.The concerns come as the INDIA bloc prepares for a major show of strength in the national capital over alleged "vote chori" and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The opposition alliance has called the November 1 rally to step up pressure on the government and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The rally follows a series of demonstrations by opposition parties over the electoral-roll revision exercise.On October 12, opposition leaders, including Gandhi, joined activists and civil society members in a 'March for Democracy' along a heavily barricaded route near the Supreme Court in Delhi. A joint petition challenging the SIR was also filed.A day later, Gandhi hosted INDIA bloc leaders for tea at his residence. Following the meeting, the opposition alliance vowed to continue its campaign and take the fight to its logical conclusion.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Cyclone Arnab: Landfall weakens to 'severe' cyclonic storm after crossing Andhra Pradesh-Yanam coast; 20,000 evacuated, trees uprooted, power cut in Konaseema, Kakinada
articles.summary: VISAKHAPATNAM/KAKINADA/AMALAPURAM: Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts on Wednesday morning and weakened from a very severe cyclonic
articles.body: VISAKHAPATNAM/KAKINADA/AMALAPURAM: Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts on Wednesday morning and weakened from a very severe cyclonic storm into a severe cyclonic storm, bringing heavy to extremely heavy rainfall, uprooting hundreds of trees and electric poles, disrupting power supply and communication, and damaging roads and standing crops across coastal districts.There were no reported casualties apart from a death due to electrocution in Visakhapatnam city. More than 20,000 people were evacuated from coastal districts before the cyclone made landfall.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the landfall process began around 1.20am on Wednesday and was completed by 9am, with the weather system moving entirely over land. Peak wind speeds reached 135 kmph, with gusts of up to 150 kmph.The cyclone crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts southwest of Yanam, about 20km east-northeast of Narsapur, 40km southwest of Yanam and 60km southwest of Kakinada. Precautionary measures taken by the administration helped limit casualties in the state.Konaseema was among the worst-affected districts, with winds reaching up to 130 kmph. Trees and electric poles were uprooted, while standing paddy and horticulture crops were damaged. Roads were blocked, and power supply and communication were disrupted.Preliminary estimates indicated that hundreds of trees and around 100 electric poles had been uprooted in Kakinada district. No major damage was reported, and rainfall subsided after 2am on Wednesday. The Uppada coastal road in the district was completely washed away.In Visakhapatnam, hundreds of trees were uprooted and several low-lying areas experienced waterlogging. The city recorded more than 20cm of rainfall in 24 hours.Electricity connections in parts of the state were expected to be restored by Wednesday evening, while major highways were expected to be cleared within hours.Two National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and two State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams had been deployed a day before the cyclone to undertake road clearance and rescue operations in response to emergency calls.In Alluri Sitharama Raju district, an old bridge at Tadiguda village in Anantagiri mandal was washed away. No injuries or casualties were reported in the incident.The IMD said the system was moving northwestwards and was centred about 20km east-northeast of Narsapur, 40km southwest of Yanam, 60km southwest of Kakinada, 90km east-northeast of Machilipatnam, 120km east of Gannavaram and 120km southwest of Tuni.It was very likely to move north-northwestwards over the next 48 hours and weaken gradually.
